hypothesis: Patients with positive or close surgical margins have shorter disease-free survival than those with negative margins.

experiment_plan.objective: Robustly evaluate the association between surgical margin status and disease-free survival, ensuring adequate sample size for Cox modeling and meeting assumption checks.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Load ‘cleaned_clinical_data.csv’ into a DataFrame.
2. Retain all patients with non-missing ‘surgical_margin’ and with at least one follow-up time: use ‘days_to_new_tumor’ when a new tumor event is recorded (‘YES’), otherwise treat missing ‘new_tumor_event’ or ‘NO’ as censored at ‘days_to_last_followup’.  
3. Recode surgical margins into two groups: Negative vs. Positive/Close.  
4. For each patient define:  
   • time = days_to_new_tumor if new_tumor_event==’YES’, else days_to_last_followup  
   • event = 1 if new_tumor_event==’YES’, else 0  
5. Check group counts; ensure each margin group has sufficient sample size (e.g., >50 patients per group). If Positive/Close still too small (<20), report counts and limit further modeling to univariate.  
6. Kaplan–Meier analysis:  
   • Fit and plot survival curves for Negative vs Positive/Close.  
   • Conduct log-rank test and report p-value.  
7. Cox proportional hazards regression:  
   a. Univariate model: margin_group as predictor.  
   b. Multivariable model: adjust for age_at_diagnosis and a simplified pathologic_stage (collapse into Stage I–II vs III–IV).  
   c. To ensure convergence and reduce collinearity, apply an L2 penalizer (e.g., penalizer=0.1).  
8. Extract hazard ratios (HR), 95% confidence intervals, and p-values for margin_group and covariates.  
9. Check proportional hazards assumptions (e.g., Schoenfeld residuals) for key variables; if violated, report results stratified or include time‐interaction term.  

Deliverables:
• Table of group sample sizes and median disease-free survival times for each margin group.  
• Kaplan–Meier plot with confidence intervals and log-rank p-value.  
• Cox regression summaries: univariate and multivariable models with HRs, CIs, and p-values.  
• Diagnostics on proportional hazards assumptions (test statistics, plots or summary).  
• Narrative interpretation of whether positive/close margins confer significantly shorter disease-free survival.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
1. Summary table: counts and median survival by margin group.  
2. Kaplan–Meier survival plot with log-rank test annotation.  
3. Univariate and multivariable Cox model output (HRs, 95% CIs, p-values).  
4. PH assumption diagnostics report.  
5. Written interpretation of findings regarding the impact of surgical margins on disease-free survival.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
# Filter for non-missing margin and follow-up time
df = df[df['surgical_margin'].notna() & df['days_to_last_followup'].notna()].copy()
# Define groups
df['margin_group'] = df['surgical_margin'].apply(lambda x: 'Negative' if x == 'Negative' else 'Positive/Close')
# Define event and time
df['event'] = (df['new_tumor_event'] == 'YES').astype(int)
# Exclude events missing days_to_new_tumor
df = df[~((df['event'] == 1) & df['days_to_new_tumor'].isna())]
df['time'] = np.where(df['event'] == 1, df['days_to_new_tumor'], df['days_to_last_followup'])

# Sample size and median table
group_counts = df['margin_group'].value_counts()
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
median_survival = {}
for grp, sub in df.groupby('margin_group'):
    kmf.fit(sub['time'], sub['event'])
    median_survival[grp] = kmf.median_survival_time_
print("Sample sizes by margin group:")
print(group_counts.to_string(), '\n')
print("Median disease-free survival (days):")
for grp, med in median_survival.items():
    print(f"  {grp}: {med:.1f}")

# Kaplan-Meier curves
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
for grp, sub in df.groupby('margin_group'):
    KaplanMeierFitter().fit(sub['time'], sub['event'], label=grp).plot(ci_show=True)
plt.title('Disease-Free Survival by Surgical Margin')
plt.xlabel('Time (days)')
plt.ylabel('Survival Probability')
# Log-rank test
grps = df['margin_group'].unique()
lr = logrank_test(
    df.loc[df['margin_group'] == grps[0], 'time'],
    df.loc[df['margin_group'] == grps[1], 'time'],
    event_observed_A=df.loc[df['margin_group'] == grps[0], 'event'],
    event_observed_B=df.loc[df['margin_group'] == grps[1], 'event']
)
plt.annotate(f"Log-rank p = {lr.p_value:.4f}", xy=(0.6, 0.1), xycoords='axes fraction')
plt.show()
print(f"Log-rank test p-value: {lr.p_value:.4f}\n")

# Cox regression: setup
# Simplify pathologic_stage
def simplify_stage(x):
    if pd.isna(x): return np.nan
    if x.startswith('Stage I') or x.startswith('Stage II'): return 'I–II'
    if x.startswith('Stage III') or x.startswith('Stage IV'): return 'III–IV'
    return np.nan

df['stage_simple'] = df['pathologic_stage'].apply(simplify_stage)
# Prepare Cox data
cox_df = df[['time', 'event', 'margin_group', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'stage_simple']].copy()
# Drop missing for multivariable
cox_df = cox_df.dropna()
# One-hot encode
cox_df = pd.get_dummies(cox_df, columns=['margin_group', 'stage_simple'], drop_first=True)

# Univariate Cox
cph_uni = CoxPHFitter(penalizer=0.1)
cph_uni.fit(cox_df[['time','event','margin_group_Positive/Close']], 'time', 'event')
print("Univariate Cox model (margin_group):")
print(cph_uni.summary, '\n')

# Multivariable Cox if adequate size
if group_counts.min() >= 20:
    cph_multi = CoxPHFitter(penalizer=0.1)
    cph_multi.fit(
        cox_df, duration_col='time', event_col='event',
        show_progress=False
    )
    print("Multivariable Cox model:")
    print(cph_multi.summary, '\n')
    print("Proportional hazards assumptions check:")
    cph_multi.check_assumptions(cox_df, show_plots=False)
else:
    print("Group sizes too small for reliable multivariable Cox regression (min group < 20). Skipping multivariable model.")

import numpy as np

from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter

# Filter relevant records
mask = (
    df['surgical_margin'].isin(['Negative', 'Positive', 'Close']) &
    df['new_tumor_event'].notna() &
    df['days_to_new_tumor'].notna() &
    df['days_to_last_followup'].notna()
)
df = df[mask].copy()
# Define groups

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
# Filter for non-missing margin and follow-up time
df = df[df['surgical_margin'].notna() & df['days_to_last_followup'].notna()].copy()
# Define groups
df['margin_group'] = df['surgical_margin'].apply(lambda x: 'Negative' if x == 'Negative' else 'Positive/Close')
# Define event and time
df['event'] = (df['new_tumor_event'] == 'YES').astype(int)
# Exclude events missing days_to_new_tumor
df = df[~((df['event'] == 1) & df['days_to_new_tumor'].isna())]
df['time'] = np.where(df['event'] == 1, df['days_to_new_tumor'], df['days_to_last_followup'])

# Sample size and median table
group_counts = df['margin_group'].value_counts()
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
median_survival = {}
for grp, sub in df.groupby('margin_group'):
    kmf.fit(sub['time'], sub['event'])
    median_survival[grp] = kmf.median_survival_time_
print("Sample sizes by margin group:")
print(group_counts.to_string(), '\n')
print("Median disease-free survival (days):")
for grp, med in median_survival.items():
    print(f"  {grp}: {med:.1f}")

# Kaplan-Meier curves
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
for grp, sub in df.groupby('margin_group'):
    KaplanMeierFitter().fit(sub['time'], sub['event'], label=grp).plot(ci_show=True)
plt.title('Disease-Free Survival by Surgical Margin')
plt.xlabel('Time (days)')
plt.ylabel('Survival Probability')
# Log-rank test
grps = df['margin_group'].unique()
lr = logrank_test(
    df.loc[df['margin_group'] == grps[0], 'time'],
    df.loc[df['margin_group'] == grps[1], 'time'],
    event_observed_A=df.loc[df['margin_group'] == grps[0], 'event'],
    event_observed_B=df.loc[df['margin_group'] == grps[1], 'event']
)
plt.annotate(f"Log-rank p = {lr.p_value:.4f}", xy=(0.6, 0.1), xycoords='axes fraction')
plt.show()
print(f"Log-rank test p-value: {lr.p_value:.4f}\n")

# Cox regression: setup
# Simplify pathologic_stage
def simplify_stage(x):
    if pd.isna(x): return np.nan
    if x.startswith('Stage I') or x.startswith('Stage II'): return 'I–II'
    if x.startswith('Stage III') or x.startswith('Stage IV'): return 'III–IV'
    return np.nan

df['stage_simple'] = df['pathologic_stage'].apply(simplify_stage)
# Prepare Cox data
cox_df = df[['time', 'event', 'margin_group', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'stage_simple']].copy()
# Drop missing for multivariable
cox_df = cox_df.dropna()
# One-hot encode
cox_df = pd.get_dummies(cox_df, columns=['margin_group', 'stage_simple'], drop_first=True)

# Univariate Cox
cph_uni = CoxPHFitter(penalizer=0.1)
cph_uni.fit(cox_df[['time','event','margin_group_Positive/Close']], 'time', 'event')
print("Univariate Cox model (margin_group):")
print(cph_uni.summary, '\n')

# Multivariable Cox if adequate size
if group_counts.min() >= 20:
    cph_multi = CoxPHFitter(penalizer=0.1)
    cph_multi.fit(
        cox_df, duration_col='time', event_col='event',
        show_progress=False
    )
    print("Multivariable Cox model:")
    print(cph_multi.summary, '\n')
    print("Proportional hazards assumptions check:")
    cph_multi.check_assumptions(cox_df, show_plots=False)
else:
    print("Group sizes too small for reliable multivariable Cox regression (min group < 20). Skipping multivariable model.")"}
